scope: Explicitly authorized Project archive/create, global/project Recipe create/update and bounded Project/Thread create/rename/move extensions through the single project.legacy.command@1 capability. Batch11 separately qualifies transport no-op receipts, stale-CAS denial, recognized pre-effect/mixed-move recovery, tamper fencing and backup lineage.
originalSourceLineage: No original source/capture pair or original-code reuse claim is introduced by this native extension record. Original-store behavior is exercised by isolated before/after, bytes/version/ordered-receipt oracles.
limitations: Admission requires explicit host-native actor/workspace authorization; caller-supplied actor, workspace, fingerprint, or global fingerprint is not accepted.
Project archive and Recipe create/update are bounded to the original store, strict ownership and host-computed fingerprint fences; filesystem effects stay outside SQL owner callbacks.
Recovery inspection runs before generic mixed-Recipe validation and retains pending/unknown bytes without guessing or replaying.

Historical opaque command IDs replay the original current snapshot; project.update remains a separate strict-CAS path. The Batch11 Project/Thread commands are admitted through this same capability's explicit native policy and shared journal, with authenticated Core HTTP/MCP source-oracle tests. No-op/mixed-move recovery is now qualified through public transports; other imported mutations remain fail-closed.

Batch11 trash import/restore uses the separate authenticated trash seam and existing knowledge.trash.restore v1 operation. The original 379-file regression suite remains not run; bounded tests do not establish full legacy operation or client parity.
This is not full original Project/Recipe command parity, production Knowledge Root access, or cutover qualification.
